title: vehicle-sil scenario (vehicle_sil_launch run --scenario), format 1
description: Steps that write the ECUs' inputs and check their outputs at given virtual times. This schema finds unknown keys, missing keys and values of the wrong form while you write. It cannot see the ECUs: whether a variable exists, may be written, and takes the value is what `vehicle_sil_launch check <configuration> --scenario <file>` says, and so is everything else this schema leaves open (a key written twice, the order of the times, whether a ${parameter} has a value, the variants in only). The manual is docs/scenario.md of vehicle-sil.
$comment: A new kind of step is one definition (step_<kind>, with the keys that go with it and the two keys of the time) and one line in the oneOf of definitions.step.

name.description: What the scenario is about. Shown in the output.

only.description: The variants (of the configuration) this scenario is for. Without it, the scenario is for every variant.

params.description: The default values of the scenario's parameters. A step uses one as ${name} where a value stands. The params of the configuration, then of the variant, then --param replace these.

propertyNames.description: A parameter's name: letters, digits and _ (not a digit first).

additionalProperties.description: One value: a number, true or false, or a text. It cannot use another parameter (${...}).

steps.description: What to do, in order. A step does one thing (set, ramp, wave, wait_until or expect) at its time: at_ms, or after_ms from the end of the step before it (without either: after_ms: 0).

not.description: A step has one time: at_ms or after_ms, not both.

set.description: Writes values: each variable (<participant>.<variable>) with its value. Inputs only, within the variable's range; a parameter of an ECU only at time 0.

ramp.description: Moves values in a straight line: each variable (<participant>.<variable>, an integer or a real input) with { to, over_ms } and, if wanted, from. The step ends after the longest over_ms.

to.description: The value at the end of the ramp.

over_ms.description: How long the ramp takes, in milliseconds of virtual time.

from.description: The value at the start of the ramp. Without it, the value the variable has then.

wave.description: Moves values in a shape over time: each variable (<participant>.<variable>, an input) with one shape (sine, triangle, sawtooth, square, pulse, noise, chirp, lag, chatter or points) and how long it lasts. The value depends on the virtual time since the step began and on nothing else. The step ends after the longest wave.

undersampled.description: Run this step's waves as they are, also where they change faster than their ECU steps: check then says nothing about that.

wave.description: One shape with its values, and beside it for_ms (how long) and around (the middle). A pulse, points and a chatter with bounces say themselves how long they last.

sine.description: A sine around the middle: the middle at the start, the highest value after a quarter of a period. For an integer or a real.

triangle.description: A triangle around the middle, with its corners where a sine has its highest and lowest values. For an integer or a real.

sawtooth.description: A sawtooth around the middle: each period rises in a straight line from the lowest value to the highest and jumps back. For an integer or a real.

falling.description: true: each period falls and jumps up.

square.description: A square: high from the start of each period for duty percent of it, then low. For a number, give low and high (its two values; low at the end) or amplitude (so far above and below the middle). For a bool, neither: it is true and false.

low.description: The value while it is low. Goes with high.

high.description: The value while it is high. Goes with low.

duty.description: The percent of each period for which it is high: 0 to 100. Without it, 50.

pulse.description: One value for width_ms, then back to the value the variable had when the pulse began (for a bool: the other value). For a number or a bool. No around beside it.

value.description: The value during the pulse. A bool may leave it out: true.

width_ms.description: How long the pulse lasts, in milliseconds of virtual time.

noise.description: Random values around the middle, each kept for hold_ms. The values depend on the seed and the time alone: every run gives the same ones. For an integer or a real.

amplitude.description: How far from the middle the values go at most; with distribution: gaussian, their standard deviation.

hold_ms.description: How long each value is kept, in milliseconds of virtual time.

distribution.description: uniform (evenly between the two ends; the default) or gaussian (bell shaped, never beyond 6 standard deviations).

chirp.description: A sine whose frequency goes from from_hz to to_hz over for_ms. For an integer or a real.

from_hz.description: The frequency at the start. 0 only with a linear sweep, and not both 0.

to_hz.description: The frequency at the end (after for_ms). 0 only with a linear sweep, and not both 0.

sweep.description: linear (the same number of hertz more every second; the default) or log (the same factor every second).

lag.description: Towards a value as a first-order lag goes: 63 % of the way after tau_ms, 99 % after 5 tau_ms. The variable keeps the value it has reached after for_ms. For an integer or a real.

tau_ms.description: The time constant, in milliseconds of virtual time.

from.description: The value at the start. Without it, the value the variable has then.

settle.description: true: at the end the variable is set to `to` itself.

chatter.description: A switch that bounces: to, back, to, back, ... every interval_ms, and to at the end. Give bounces (how often it falls back) here, or for_ms beside the shape. For a number or a bool.

to.description: The value it comes to rest at.

interval_ms.description: How long it stays at a value between two changes, in milliseconds of virtual time.

bounces.description: How often it falls back before it rests. The chatter then lasts 2 x bounces x interval_ms.

seed.description: With a seed the changes are not even: each up to a quarter of interval_ms early or late, the same in every run.

from.description: The value it falls back to (not for a bool). Without it, the value the variable has then.

points.description: A table: [milliseconds since the step began, value] in the order of the times. The wave ends at the last point, and the variable keeps its value. For any type; a bool and an enum keep each value until the next point.

items.description: Milliseconds of virtual time since the step began.

around.description: The middle of the shape, and the value at the end. Without it, the value the variable has when the step begins. Not for pulse, points, lag and chatter, and not for a square with low and high.

for_ms.description: How long the wave lasts, in milliseconds of virtual time. Not for a pulse (width_ms) and points (the last point).

interpolate.description: For points, beside them (not inside): linear (straight lines between the points; the default for a number) or hold (each value until the next point; the way to write a value that jumps).

amplitude.description: How far the value goes above and below the middle: 0 or more.

period_ms.description: How long one period is, in milliseconds of virtual time. Give this or frequency_hz.

frequency_hz.description: Periods per second of virtual time: more than 0. (For a shape that repeats: give this or period_ms.)

sweep_hz.description: Periods per second of virtual time: 0 or more.

phase_deg.description: Where in its period the shape begins, in degrees: 90 begins a quarter of a period in. Without it, 0.

seed.description: A whole number that picks the values: the same seed gives the same values in every run.

wait_until.description: Waits until every condition is true: each variable (<participant>.<variable>) with what it must be. Needs timeout_ms. When the step ends is not known before the run, so the steps after it take after_ms, not at_ms.

timeout_ms.description: How long wait_until waits at most, in milliseconds of virtual time. When it passes, the step fails.

not.description: within_ms (true at some time) or hold_for_ms (true all the time), not both: make a step of each.

expect.description: Checks that every condition is true: each variable (<participant>.<variable>) with what it must be. At the step's time; with within_ms, at some time within it; with hold_for_ms, all that time.

within_ms.description: expect passes as soon as the conditions are true within this many milliseconds of virtual time, and the next step follows. The steps after it take after_ms, not at_ms.

hold_for_ms.description: expect passes if the conditions stay true for this many milliseconds of virtual time.

at_ms.description: The virtual time of the step, in milliseconds. Not before the end of the step before it, and not after a step that waits (wait_until, expect with within_ms).

after_ms.description: The time of the step, in milliseconds of virtual time after the end of the step before it.

parameter.description: A parameter, ${name}, as the whole value: it reads as the parameter's value. Inside { } or [ ], write it in quotes ("${name}").

hexadecimal.description: A whole number in hexadecimal, 0x1F or 0X1F, without quotes: for a value of an integer or an enum variable only.

variable_name.description: A variable: <participant>.<variable>. The participant's name ends at the first '.'; the variable's name may have more (Engine.engine.speed).

value.description: A value of the variable's type: true or false for a bool, a whole number for an integer (decimal, or hexadecimal such as 0x1F), a number for a real, an item's name or its number for an enum. Or a parameter, ${name}.

condition.description: What the variable must be: a value (equal to it), or comparisons, all of which must hold ({ ge: 1700, le: 1900 }).

ge.description: Greater than or equal to (numbers only).

le.description: Less than or equal to (numbers only).

near.description: At most tolerance away from this value (numbers only). Needs tolerance.

tolerance.description: How far from near the value may be. Goes with near.
